correctness.rationale: Freeness on letters uniquely recovers the branch h_t from x^(t)_1 and x^(t+1)_0. The first letter at time j is (h_(j-1)…h_0) applied to the j-th initial letter. Arbitrary first letters and labels reconstruct the initial word by inverse prefix products, then the whole trajectory by the ordered recurrence. Each input/output coordinate requires only finitely many coordinates, and advancing time shifts the code. The product order needs no commutativity. Repeated words give q^n fixed trajectories, cylinder counts give log q, the formal exponential series gives (1-qt)^(-1), and Möbius inversion followed by division by least period gives the primitive orbit count. The proof includes q=1 and does not confuse fixed full trajectories with multivalued periodic states.
residual_risks: Finite test-code counts are supplementary, not an all-period certificate.

evidence: The quotient identity F(x)=π^(-1)(Tπx) and unrestricted trajectory lifts hold for finite isometric actions and any continuous equivariant f, even when the action is not free. Oliveira treats involutive-isometry shadowing and explicitly gives the binary map.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The usual product shift metric makes the frozen action isometric and the shift is equivariant. The general lift statement applies; free letters provide a continuous product trivialization of the quotient map in this example. Oliveira alone does not give the trajectory invariant.

evidence: Write a letter as (b_j,g_j) in B×H, with B=A/H and H acting on the left. The quotient of a word is coded by (b_j,g_j^(-1)g_(j+1)) at every j. These coordinates are invariant and arbitrary; the representative with g_0=e is reconstructed by cumulative right multiplication. The induced quotient shift drops the first pair. The inspected lift statement then says each successive initial group coordinate can be chosen independently, yielding the full shift on B×H×H, with |B||H|²=|A||H|.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Both coordinate reconstructions are continuous, including at all periodic sequences. Thus the pre-existing general lift relation with this elementary full-shift quotient gives the claimed topological classification and its full-shift invariants; different gauge coordinates do not change the result.

originality.rationale: A distinct Resultary record already covers the decisive stronger trajectory-lifting relation. Its proof explicitly says that every lift sequence of a quotient orbit is an actual trajectory, because the next orbit fibre is the full image. The frozen conjugacy follows directly by writing the free alphabet as B×H, coding the quotient shift by orbit letters and successive group differences, and recording one freely chosen fibre coordinate per time. This proves coverage by implication; the other result is not claimed to print the same conjugacy formula or to have priority.
residual_risks: The coverage finding does not settle chronology or priority; in particular the overlapping Resultary record carries a later date label.
Other skew-product treatments may provide equivalent direct codes.

value.rationale: Distinguishing trajectory invariants from periodic-state invariants is useful and the gauge is a clean exposition. As a distinct mathematical contribution, however, the entire finding is a routine full-shift recoding of the already established unrestricted lift relation. The entropy, zeta and orbit counts are standard consequences and leave no separately needed case or obstruction in the frozen claim.
residual_risks: This is a judgment on the stated contribution, not on the expository usefulness of the code.
